question_text: The two ends of a cylindrical rod of nickel 120.00 mm long and 12.000 mm in diameter are maintained rigid. If the rod is initially at $70^{\circ} \mathrm{C}$, to what temperature must it be cooled in order to have a $0.023-\mathrm{mm}$ reduction in diameter? The values of $v$ and $\alpha{l}$ for nickel are 0.31 and $13.3 \times 10^{-6}\left({ }^{\circ} \mathrm{C}\right)^{-1}$, respectively.The unit of the answer is ${}^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$.
response:
**Calculation:**

$$\Delta T = \frac{\Delta d / d}{\alpha_l(1+\nu)} = \frac{-0.023/12.000}{13.3\times10^{-6}\times 1.31} = -110.0\,°\mathrm{C}$$

$$T = 70 + (-110.0) = -40.0\,°\mathrm{C}$$

The rod must be cooled to a temperature of:

$$\boxed{-40.0}$$
